subject: Startups
title: The Rise of Solo Capitalists
description: One-minute skill: The Rise of Solo Capitalists.

hook.text: A new breed of investors works alone—no partners, no committees, no delays. They're called solo capitalists.

buildup.text: Investors like Elad Gil and Lachy Groom run billion-dollar funds with tiny teams. Decisions take hours, not weeks.

discovery.text: Solo capitalists win deals by moving fast. Founders prefer one person who decides quickly over a slow committee.

twist.text: But solo capitalists can't offer the platform services of a16z or the network of Sequoia. Speed has limits.

climax.text: The VC landscape is splitting: massive platform firms on one end, fast solo operators on the other.

punchline.text: One person, one fund, one fast decision. No committee.

quiz.question: What advantage do solo capitalists have over traditional VC firms?
